maintainedBy.manager: owns this register: milestone ids, sequence, status transitions, ownership, boundaries and the merge protocol
maintainedBy.agent-2: owns the backend evidence rows (implementation, backend tests, contract publication) and may not re-sequence
maintainedBy.agent-1: owns the frontend evidence rows (consumption, frontend tests, vocabulary alignment) and may not re-sequence
maintainedBy.rule: An agent may add evidence to the milestone it is assigned and may propose a status change. Only the manager changes an id, a sequence, a boundary or a status of record.

description: The canonical, machine-readable MILESTONE layer of this repository: the granular P2.x steps beneath the strategic Phase A-F roadmap, with owner, dependencies, inputs, deliverables, implementation boundary, gates, decision dependencies, completion criteria, start/finish evidence, the commit each row was verified against, and the milestone that follows it. It exists so a new agent with no chat history can answer: what the previous milestone delivered, why this one is next, what it owns, what it deliberately does NOT implement, what comes after it, which dependencies block later work, and which gates define completion. It is a register, not a narrative: every claim here names the file or command that proves it.
createdIn: P2.13 (Part A - milestone reconciliation). Before this file the repository's roadmap was coarse (Phase A-F in manifest/ai-lego-set.json plus prose in docs/n8n-lego/ROADMAP.md), which is why the generated status documents still said 'Current phase P2.11' after P2.12 had shipped.

productTruth.rule: Where this register and a manifest disagree about a NUMBER (domains, capabilities, operations, contracts, error codes), the manifest wins and the row here is a defect. Read the generated .ai/master/CURRENT_STATUS.md for live counts.

decisions.rule: A milestone may not resolve a decision. decisionDependencies below name the rows that gate a milestone; the arbiter named in each row decides it.

They are named here so a dependency on them resolves, and they are NOT retro-fitted with deliverables or evidence that nobody recorded at the time.

statusVocabulary.planned: sequenced, not started; no branch work and no implementation evidence
statusVocabulary.ready: dependencies published and no open decision blocks it; work may start
statusVocabulary.in-progress: an assigned agent is implementing it on its branch
statusVocabulary.blocked: a named dependency or decision prevents progress; the blocker is recorded, not implied
statusVocabulary.complete: delivered, gated and reconciled on protected main; evidence recorded
statusVocabulary.superseded: replaced by another milestone; the row is kept with a pointer, never deleted
statusVocabulary.rule: These six words are the whole status vocabulary and no other status word is valid. 'Almost done', 'ready-ish' and 'done on my branch' are not statuses: agent completion is recorded in statusBySide, and only reconciliation on protected main makes a milestone complete.

policy.idRefinement: Future milestone ids below P2.13 are INDICATIVE (each carries idStatus: 'indicative'). The manager may split, merge, re-sequence or renumber a future milestone - for example if implementation evidence shows Memory must be two milestones - but ONLY by updating this register in the same change that records the reason. An id that moved keeps its old row with status 'superseded' and a 'supersededBy' pointer.
policy.noInventedReadiness: A milestone is never marked ready because it is convenient. 'ready' requires every dependency to be published (a contract-lock row, a registered capability, or a declared manifest block) and every blocking decision to be closed. Where a dependency is declared but not published, the row says so in blockingDecisions.
policy.historyRule: Historical evidence is never rewritten to look current. A completed milestone keeps the commit it was verified against, the counts that were true then, and the decisions as they stood. Corrections are additive: a 'corrections' or 'supersededNotice' field on the row, plus the current canonical state - never an edited past.
policy.scopeRule: A milestone's 'boundary.mustNot' list is part of its definition. Implementing something on that list is a scope violation, and the correct action at reconciliation is to not merge that scope - not to merge it and clean up later.
policy.architectureFirst: Architecture -> Contract -> Test -> Implementation, in that order, for every milestone. A milestone that reaches implementation before its contract is locked records the gap as a decision row (P2.13's is XA-20) instead of inventing the contract locally.

mergeProtocol.summary: An agent branch is not the milestone. The reconciled, verified state on protected main is the milestone.
mergeProtocol.agentCompletionIsNotMergeApproval: 'My branch is complete' means: the assigned implementation is complete, its focused tests pass, the branch is internally consistent and its evidence is published. It does NOT mean the branch is safe to merge. The manager owns that decision.
sequence: manager reconciliation: compare both branches against the same main baseline, inspect the shared contract surface, detect drift and conflicts, verify dependency assumptions, run cross-agent alignment tests, regenerate .ai if required, verify documentation and status
post-merge verification: same expected tree, same contract lock, same generated .ai state, tests pass on main HEAD

twoGates.reconciliationPass: the two agent outputs are mutually consistent and compatible with the architecture
twoGates.mergePass: the reconciled state passed the required validation against the actual target main
twoGates.why: 'The branches were reconciled' is not 'the milestone is complete'. Treating them as one gate is the failure mode this protocol exists to prevent.

reconcileChecks.baseline: BASE = current protected main. Both branches are understood as BASE + agent-1 changes and BASE + agent-2 changes; never 'merge whichever arrives first'.
reconcileChecks.contractAuthority: backend contract -> canonical schema / operations / errors / permissions -> frontend consumer. The manager verifies agent-1 did not redefine anything agent-2 owns, and that the frontend is not a parallel interpretation of the same concept.
reconcileChecks.architectureDrift: duplicate LEGO domains, duplicate contracts, renamed concepts diverging from canonical vocabulary, future-scope components implemented early, accidental runtime dependencies, new authority or permission paths, hidden coupling, and architecture decisions made implicitly in code.
reconcileChecks.testReconciliation: agent-1 focused tests PASS, agent-2 focused tests PASS, shared contract tests PASS, cross-agent alignment PASS, full relevant suite PASS. The last two are the gate; the first two are not sufficient.

conflictTypes.action: NOT a normal merge conflict: the contract is reconciled first, then the code follows it

conflictTypes.name: architecture

conflictTypes.action: do not merge that scope - not 'merge now and clean it up later'

onFailure.then: agent correction -> reconciliation again. Never a silent merge, and never a merge of a locked-contract disagreement.

mergeProtocol.mergeAuthority: Only the manager turns agent branches into product state on main. Agents do not merge to main, do not force-push, and do not reset another agent's branch to make a tree look synchronized.
mergeProtocol.appliesTo: P2.13, P2.14 and every later milestone. This protocol is governance, not product architecture: it must never be referenced by manifest/domains.json, manifest/ai-lego-set.json or any product contract.

The pin was NOT edited - a gate is not edited to make a run green - so the check is reported FAIL with its measurement and escalated as XA-21 / B-14. docs/n8n-lego/evidence/frontend-boundary-p213-run.json is this run; frontend-boundary-p25.json is left as captured at P2.5 because re-capturing it here would replace three environmental PASS rows with FAILs.

The Context & Session view is built on demand rather than eagerly at assembly: it is not part of the boot descriptor, and the boot path should not pay for a surface nobody has rendered. A handed-over record is still validated at the boundary (fail-closed is not deferred); only the empty case is lazy. This holds the probe at ~4.25 MB instead of ~4.36 MB and is recorded here because it is a design choice a reconciler should see.
